metadata.summary: Monaco have pulled out of the deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea - who feel the French club have acted in an extraordinary and deeply unprofessional way.
metadata.content: Lamine Camara: Monaco pull out of selling midfielder to Chelsea in £47m deal after Blues agreed deal for Enzo Fernandez replacement | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Lamine Camara: Monaco pull out of selling midfielder to Chelsea in £47m deal after Blues agreed deal for Enzo Fernandez replacement Chelsea were looking for a midfield addition after letting Enzo Fernandez join Manchester City in a £125m deal, which is a joint-record for a British club; Monaco pulled out because they successfully renegotiated a deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton Kaveh Solhekol Chief Correspondent Tuesday 1 September 2026 23:37, UK Image: Chelsea have agreed a deal to sign Monaco's Lamine Camara Monaco have pulled out of the deal to sell Lamine Camara to Chelsea - who feel the French club have acted in an extraordinary and deeply unprofessional way. Camara was set to join Chelsea for £47m and was to sign a six-year deal pending a medical. Just after the 11pm transfer deadline passed, news emerged that Monaco reneged on the agreement they had with Chelsea, and they had informed the Blues of their decision in writing. The reason for Monaco pulling out was that they had successfully renegotiated the deal to sell Folarin Balogun to Everton. There was a full written club-to-club agreement with Chelsea to complete the Camara deal. messages.text: Man City sign Fernandez in British-record-equalling deal

metadata.summary: Manchester City have signed Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for a joint-British-record fee of £125m.
metadata.content: Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City sign midfielder from Chelsea in British-record-equalling £125m deal | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Man City sign midfielder from Chelsea in British-record-equalling £125m deal Tuesday 1 September 2026 23:34, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Jamie Carragher believes the signing of Enzo Fernandez will make Man City Arsenal's biggest title challenger Manchester City have signed Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea for a joint-British-record fee of £125m. The size of the fee matches the amount Liverpool paid Newcastle for Alexander Isak on Deadline Day a year ago. The Fernandez deal comes amid Chelsea fury that Monaco pulled out on selling Lamine Camara - who was deemed as the Argentine's replacement - in the final minutes of the window. Chelsea had the option of pulling the plug on Fernandez to Man City after the Camara deal collapsed - but they stuck to their word and honoured their commitment to complete the deal. Fernandez's Deadline Day move comes more than three months after the Argentina international first told Chelsea he wanted to leave, and more than two weeks after the club imposed a deadline for bids.
